title: EIP-7862: Delayed State Root
description: Separate state root computation from block validation
author: Charlie Noyes <charlie@paradigm.xyz>, Dan Robinson <dan@paradigm.xyz>, Justin Drake <justin@ethereum.org>, Toni Wahrstätter (@nerolation)
laymanDescription: Before a block can be accepted, someone has to compute a fingerprint summarizing all of Ethereum's data after that block runs, and this is one of the slowest steps in producing a block. This proposal shifts that fingerprint one block later, so each block carries the previous block's result and validators no longer wait on it.
benefits: Takes state root computation off the critical path between block production and attestation
Builders compute one state root per slot instead of thousands during the auction window
Lets block access list data parallelize state root computation, which is impossible today
tradeoffs: State proofs for a block become available only one slot later, affecting light clients
Clients must track and recompute the last state root across reorgs
Reuses the existing header field with new meaning, so anything reading it must be updated
